Jordan: Heads-up — ran a longtrace with nsys on the regression repro (longseq=12k, microbatch=2) and saw HBM hit sustained saturation followed by a kernel selection fallback that killed throughput. timeline + nvlink shows big memcpy stalls around the KV read path. anyone seen alloc / eviction-induced kernel falls like this? :thinking:

Priya: Can you paste the exact nsys command and a short timeline snippet? and link to perfetto if you uploaded it. :eyes:

Jordan: Sure — command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,cuda_memsync --output=/tmp/kv-3012345678 --force-overwrite --sample=cpu 
  --duration=60 --target-processes=all --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi 
  --capture-range-end=none python -m rw_infer.bench --model xlarge --seqlen 12000 --batch 2 --microbatch 2
```
Quick timeline excerpt (nsys timeline collapsed):
- 0s: warmup kernels (fast_gemm_fp16)
- 2.1s: sustained kv_read / kv_decompress kernels start spiking memcpy and atomic ops
- 2.3s: runtime switches to fallback kernel set (generic_gemm_bf16_split) — per-kernel latencies + memory ops jump ~3x
- 2.3s-10s: HBM bandwidth sits at 580-610 GB/s, SM util drops, DMA stalls climb

perf-bot: automated analysis: detected 1) HBM >= 85% for a sustained window, 2) 72% of device-side stalls attributed to async memcpy/kv_read path, 3) increased CUDA kernel launch latency after allocator pressure events. Recommend checking KV page eviction rate and host->device copy batching.

Alex: This smells like allocator/eviction thrash. When KV cache evicts many pages you get scatter frees -> allocator slowpath -> the runtime may choose safer (slower) kernels because the memory fragmentation/placement changed. Two quick experiments:
1) Force large page size / reduce page churn: set RW_KV_PAGE_SIZE=4194304 and RW_KV_PREFETCH_WINDOW=16 (env)
2) Restrict sequence cap to observe kernel choice: run same trace with --seqlen-cap 2048

Drew: Also try reproducing with microbatching turned off to see if batching heuristics are contributing to kernel fallback. e.g. set RW_BATCHER_MICRO=0 and run a short nsys. If fallback still occurs, it's likely allocator/placement not batching. Also collect a short nvprof with kernel names + attributes.

Sam: Another angle — kernel selection heuristics in our GEMM chooser use tile rounding that depends on token block counts. For very long seqlen we sometimes cross a boundary where the heuristic prefers a tiled kernel that requires more temporary buffers -> pushes us past an HBM placement threshold and triggers different allocation path. Quick test: run small script to print chosen kernel for each step (we have a flag):
```
export RW_RUNTIME_DEBUG_KERNELS=1
python -m rw_infer.run --model xlarge --seqlen 12000 --batch 1 --log-kernel-choices > kernel-log.txt
```
Look for when choice flips from fast_gemm_fp16 -> generic_gemm_bf16_split.

Jordan: Good suggestions. Action plan I'm taking now:
- Re-run with RW_KV_PAGE_SIZE=4MB + RW_KV_PREFETCH_WINDOW=32 and microbatch off, capture 30s nsys (shorter).
- Run the kernel-choices debug to get a step-by-step map.
- Upload perfetto timeline and nvprof slice if we still see fallback.

Priya: If you can repro quickly, add one run with pinned allocator (experimental flag RW_ALLOC_PIN=1). If that prevents fallback we'll know it's placement fragmentation.

Jordan: running now (kicking off the jobs). will paste perfetto link + kernel-log when done. thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: job queued: nsys -> /artifacts/kv-3012345678/ (will post perfetto link when conversion completes)

Drew: one more nit: capture metrics with `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` alongside profiling to correlate HBM with SM util and PCIe traffic. often the DMA vs memcpy shape tells the story.

Jordan: got the first short run: perfetto link https://perfetto.dev/trace/ui/abcdefgh - kernel-log shows flip at iteration 14, pinning allocator avoided the flip on a second run. saving traces now.

Sam: Nice — that strongly points to allocator/placement. next steps: replicate on a second GPU model (A100 vs H100) to see if the kernel chooser differs by device capabilities and bandwidth headroom.

Jordan: adding that to the run matrix. closing this thread after I upload final artifacts. cheers.
